==English==

===Etymology===
From {{inh|en|enm|rebuken}}, from {{der|en|xno|rebuker|t=to beat back, {{l|en|repel}}}}, from {{m|fro|re-}} + {{der|en|fro|*buker}}, {{m|fro|buchier}}, {{m|fro|buschier|t=to strike, hack down, chop}}, from {{m|fro|busche|t=wood}}, from {{der|en|la-vul|*busca|t=wood, grove}}, from {{der|en|frk|*busk||grove}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*buskaz|t=bush}}; equivalent to {{prefix|en|re-|bush}}.

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/ɹiˈbjuːk/|/ɹɪˈbjuːk/}}
* {{audio|en|en-us-rebuke.ogg|a=US}}
* {{rhymes|en|uːk|s=2}}

===Noun===
{{en-noun}}

# {{lb|en|of a person}} A [[harsh]] [[criticism]].
#* {{quote-journal|en|date=2012 July 15|author=Richard Williams|work=w:Guardian Unlimited|url=http://www.guardian.co.uk/sport/2012/jul/15/tour-de-france-2012-bradley-wiggins|title=Tour de France 2012: Carpet tacks cannot force Bradley Wiggins off track|text=There was the sternness of an old-fashioned Tour ''patron'' in his '''rebuke''' to the young Frenchman Pierre Rolland, the only one to ride away from the peloton and seize the opportunity for a lone attack before being absorbed back into the bunch, where he was received with coolness.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20220625161920/https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2012/jul/15/tour-de-france-2012-bradley-wiggins}}
#* {{RQ:en:Christian Science Monitor|date=2025-04-19|author=Nicole Winfield|title=JD Vance visits the Vatican for Easter after papal rebuke over Trump's migrant crackdown|url=https://www.csmonitor.com/USA/Politics/2025/0419/jd-vance-vatican-pope-easter-trump-immigration|passage=U.S. Vice President JD Vance met Saturday with the Vatican's No. 2 official, following a remarkable papal '''rebuke''' of the Trump administration’s crackdown on migrants and Vance’s theological justification of it.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20250428134726/https://www.csmonitor.com/USA/Politics/2025/0419/jd-vance-vatican-pope-easter-trump-immigration}}
#* {{RQ:Guardian|date=2025-04-21|author=Peter Stanford|url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2025/apr/21/pope-francis-obituary|title=Pope Francis obituary|passage=With his emphasis on accepting the science (he was a trained chemist) – and hence his stern '''rebuke''' to the climate change deniers and the politicians who courted them – he even managed to reset the relationship between science and religion, which had been rocky ever since Galileo fell foul of the Inquisition 400 years earlier.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20250430033924/https://www.theguardian.com/world/2025/apr/21/pope-francis-obituary}}

===Verb===
{{en-verb}}

# {{lb|en|of a person}} To [[criticise]] [[harsh]]ly; to [[reprove]].
#: {{syn|en|reprimand|reproach|reprove|reprehend|admonish|Thesaurus:criticize}}
#* {{RQ:New International Version|Psalm|6|text=O Lord, do not '''rebuke''' me in Your anger or discipline me in Your wrath.}}
#* {{RQ:Guardian|date=2 Feb 2021|author=Katharine Murphy|url=https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/commentisfree/2021/feb/02/scott-morrison-must-heed-the-lesson-of-donald-trump-and-slap-down-craig-kelly|
text=When Morrison mulls the pluses and minuses associated with '''rebuking''' Kelly for undermining the government’s public health messaging, the prime minister faces a genuine substantive dilemma, and that goes to the risks of amplification.|title=Scott Morrison must heed the lesson of Donald Trump and slap down Craig Kelly|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20210427091242/https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/commentisfree/2021/feb/02/scott-morrison-must-heed-the-lesson-of-donald-trump-and-slap-down-craig-kelly}}
